intro: Ninth beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows.

items.text: **Full-screen captures get the background** when "Background on by default" is on: in the copy, the floating preview and history (Edit can still change it).
**Numbered steps:** set the badge outline (color, width) and shadow in Settings → Tools.
**Dim color:** pick the color capture mode dims the screen with (Settings → Appearance; black by default).
**History:** "Recording" switch in Settings → General, matching the History window and the menu-bar menu.
**Windows:** the History window has a close button, and dropdown lists in Settings are readable in the dark themes.
**Clearer wording:** shorter descriptions throughout Settings, tooltips and dialogs.

intro: Eighth beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows. A small Windows fix.

items.text: **Windows: the app is called "Snapkit" everywhere.** Startup apps, Task Manager and Installed apps showed Snapkit's long description ("Minimal, fully customizable screenshot tool…") as its name and "Son" as its publisher. Both are now simply **Snapkit**.

intro: Seventh beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows.

items.text: **New home on GitHub:** Snapkit now lives at **github.com/an-ordinary-melody/snapkit** (the GitHub account was renamed). This beta checks for updates there. Older betas still find updates through GitHub's redirect from the old address, but please install this one so update checks go straight to the new home.

intro: Sixth beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows. A Windows fix.

items.text: **Windows: the floating preview stays on top after an area capture.** With the floating preview on, the preview was created after copying but ended up behind the window you went back to (it only showed after minimizing something). It now stays on top, as it already did after a full-screen capture.
Behind the scenes: a Windows test now asks Windows itself whether the preview is on top of the app you return to, at 100% and 150% display scaling.

intro: Fifth beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows.

items.text: **New look:** Snapkit has its own icon now, the snapping hand. On macOS 26 and later the app icon is a real Liquid Glass icon (light, dark and tinted looks); older macOS and Windows get the same icon flat. The menu-bar icon (Mac) and tray icon (Windows) use it too.
**Quick area capture** (Settings → General → After a capture, off by default): the area you draw is copied the moment you let go, with no adjusting or drawing step.
**Editor zoom, continued:**
sub: On a Mac, scrolling up (⌘ + scroll) now zooms in, like on Windows; a trackpad pinch works as before.
Hold **Space** and drag to move around a zoomed-in image, like Photoshop's hand tool.
Fast scrolling or pinching zooms the full amount (quick steps used to be partly lost).

items.text: **Scrollbars** are thin and rounded with no background strip, in the theme's colors (the settings window had a white strip in the dark theme).

intro: Fourth beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows.

items.text: **Zoom in the background editor:** Ctrl + scroll zooms the preview around the mouse pointer (on a Mac also ⌘ + scroll or a trackpad pinch), and you can scroll around when zoomed in. **Ctrl + 0** (⌘0) fits it back to the window; Ctrl + / Ctrl − zoom in steps, and the % badge in the corner also fits. The image and your drawings are redrawn sharp at every zoom level.
**Windows: text is 26 px by default** (was 32). macOS stays at 20 px. Changeable in Settings → Tools.

intro: Third beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows. This one is mostly Windows fixes.

items.text: **Shortcuts held by another app now come back.** If another app is using one of Snapkit's shortcuts, Snapkit keeps trying and takes it as soon as that app quits (before, it stayed dead until Snapkit restarted). Settings → Shortcuts marks a shortcut another app holds right now, and a taken capture shortcut at startup shows a notification instead of a blocking error box.
**Editor on small or scaled screens (e.g. Windows at 150%):** the editor's tools no longer run past its edges, where they couldn't be clicked; they wrap onto a second row.
**Windows: text is 32 px by default** (easier to read at Windows' usual display scaling). macOS stays at 20 px. Changeable in Settings → Tools.
Behind the scenes: the end-to-end tests now also run on Windows, at 100% and 150% display scaling.

intro: Second beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows.

items.text: **Smaller downloads:** the Mac installer is 77 MB (was 93 MB) and the Windows installer 71 MB (was 78 MB). Snapkit now ships only Chromium's English language files and uses stronger DMG compression.
**Full-screen capture is now `⌘⇧9`** (was `⌘⇧5`, which is also macOS's own screenshot toolbar). If you never changed it, it switches by itself; you can pick another in Settings → Shortcuts.
Behind the scenes: an end-to-end test run with about 100 checks, one for each bug fixed so far, now has to pass before every release.

intro: First public beta of Snapkit, a fast screenshot tool for macOS and Windows: hotkey → frozen screen → select → annotate → ⌘C.

items.text: **Capture:** `⌥⇧Z` for an area, `⌘⇧5` for the whole screen (straight to the floating preview), from the menu bar too.
**Annotate:** pencil, arrows (one-way or two-way), shapes, highlighter, text, numbered steps and blur. Smart alignment while moving; edit text in place.
**Background:** gradient, color or image backgrounds with padding, corners, shadow and fixed output sizes.
**Floating preview and pins:** copy, edit or pin the last capture; pins float above everything.
**History:** `⌘⇧1` opens your recent captures (copy again, edit, pin, save, star, drag out as a file). Keeps 10 by default, up to 30.
**Settings:** `⌘⇧2`. Light, Gray, Dark or System theme, optional Liquid Glass, every shortcut and tool configurable.
Launch at login and update notifications (this beta is offered newer betas).
